requirements.text: The final risk parameter estimate consists of the best estimate, including appropriate adjustments, plus the margin of conservatism.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CRM-STD-101 v2.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The MoC is not used to compensate for deficiencies that can be corrected through an appropriate adjustment.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CRM-STD-101 v2.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The MoC distinguishes category A (data and methodological deficiencies), category B (relevant changes) and category C (general estimation error).
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text; categories consistent with EBA/GL/2017/16 section 4.4.

requirements.text: Each identified deficiency is linked to exactly one category (A or B) and recorded in the MoC register with a unique identifier, the affected parameters and segments, and a reference to the MRM-STD-022 data deficiency log.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CRM-STD-101 v2.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Each deficiency is quantified individually as its effect on the risk parameter per calibration segment before aggregation within its category.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CRM-STD-101 v2.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The quantification of each category A and B deficiency is supported by a sensitivity analysis that re-estimates the parameter under plausible alternative treatments of the deficiency.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CRM-STD-101 v2.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The MoC for a deficiency is not lower than the adverse effect indicated by the sensitivity analysis, unless a lower value is justified and approved by Model Risk Management.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CRM-STD-101 v2.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Deficiencies are identified systematically at each development, recalibration and annual review using the trigger list of Annex 1.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CRM-STD-101 v2.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Deficiencies identified by validation, monitoring, internal audit or the supervisor are assessed for their effect on the estimates and, where relevant, added to the MoC register within three months.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CRM-STD-101 v2.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: For each deficiency an appropriate adjustment is considered first, and the remaining uncertainty of any adjustment applied is assessed for category A MoC.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CRM-STD-101 v2.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The deficiency assessment, including deficiencies considered and rejected, is documented in the MoC section of the model development document.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CRM-STD-101 v2.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The MoC is quantified at least per category and per calibration segment (or per grade for PD).
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CRM-STD-101 v2.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Expert judgement is used to quantify MoC only where sensitivity, bootstrap or scenario, and benchmarking methods are not feasible, and is documented and approved under MRM-STD-023.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CRM-STD-101 v2.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The sensitivity analysis documents the plausible range of each alternative treatment, the parameter value under each treatment and the rationale for the value selected.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CRM-STD-101 v2.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The MoC for each deficiency is non-negative, and a deficiency that lowers the estimate does not reduce the MoC of other deficiencies.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CRM-STD-101 v2.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Category C MoC for PD is at least the difference between the upper bound of a one-sided 90% confidence interval of the LRA default rate and the LRA, accounting for autocorrelation of yearly default rates.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to PD rating systems only.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CRM-STD-101 v2.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Category C MoC for LGD and CCF is at least the difference between the 90th percentile of the bootstrapped long-run average and the long-run average.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to LGD and CCF models only.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CRM-STD-101 v2.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The total MoC per calibration segment is the simple sum of the category A, B and C MoCs, without diversification.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CRM-STD-101 v2.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: For PD the MoC is applied to the calibrated best estimate before the regulatory floor; for LGD and CCF the order of adjustments, MoC and downturn is documented and applied consistently in development and production.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CRM-STD-101 v2.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The application of MoC preserves rank ordering, with PDs after MoC increasing monotonically with grade.
requirements.not_applicable_reason: Applies to PD rating systems only.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CRM-STD-101 v2.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Where IRB parameters are used for purposes requiring unbiased estimates, such as IFRS 9, the MoC is removed and the removal documented.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CRM-STD-101 v2.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The effect of the MoC on risk-weighted exposure amounts is reported per category and per rating system.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CRM-STD-101 v2.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Each category A deficiency has a remediation plan with an owner and target date, unless documented as permanent and reassessed at each annual review.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CRM-STD-101 v2.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Where the total MoC exceeds 20% of the best estimate for PD, or 5 percentage points for LGD or CCF, the need for redevelopment is presented to the Model Risk Committee.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CRM-STD-101 v2.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: An MoC component is reduced or removed only after remediation of the underlying deficiency has been implemented and confirmed by Model Validation.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CRM-STD-101 v2.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The MoC is reviewed at least annually as part of the annual review of estimates, including the continued relevance and quantification of each deficiency.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CRM-STD-101 v2.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The MoC register records per deficiency the category, quantification method, MoC value, calibration segments affected and remediation status, and is kept up to date.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CRM-STD-101 v2.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Changes in the MoC are classified as model changes under MRM-STD-050 and Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 529/2014.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CRM-STD-101 v2.0) text authored for the library.
